speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a psychiatric condition and a new onset movement disorder. To begin our evaluation, have you noticed any changes in your mood, anxiety levels, or sleep patterns recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding your psychiatric symptoms. However, the new onset of movement disorder requires immediate investigation; have you noticed any involuntary muscle contractions, stiffness, or tremors since starting the risperidone?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—inability to remain still, fidgeting, and repetitive leg movements—are highly suggestive of akathisia. Since you started risperidone two months ago, this is a likely adverse effect. Have you noticed if these sensations worsen at night or if you are experiencing any muscle stiffness or tremors as well?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced Akathisia secondary to Risperidone.

The clinical picture of severe restlessness, fidgeting, and inability to remain still shortly after starting risperidone is classic for akathisia. Since your psychiatric symptoms are improving, we will likely need to adjust your risperidone dosage or add a medication to treat this side effect. Do you have any other specific questions about managing this new symptom?
